speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are a pregnant patient experiencing vaginal bleeding and abdominal pain. To assess the urgency, please tell me how many weeks pregnant you are and exactly when these symptoms started?

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old woman, gravida 2, para 1, at 38 weeks' gestation. The patient reports experiencing vaginal bleeding for the past hour accompanied by severe abdominal pain. She mentions that she felt contractions before the onset of the bleeding, but the contractions ceased once the bleeding began. Her first childbirth was a cesarean section due to nonreassuring fetal heart rate.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that detail; the history of a prior C-section raises concern for uterine rupture. Have you experienced any loss of fetal movement, a sudden decrease in fetal heart tones, or any tearing sensation in your abdomen?

REQUEST TEST: Fetal Heart Rate Monitoring
REQUEST IMAGES: Ultrasound_Abdominal

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Fetal Heart Rate Monitoring: Shows recurrent variable decelerations; Ultrasound_Abdominal: Findings suggest a disruption in the uterine wall continuity adjacent to the scar from the previous cesarean section, with associated hemoperitoneum.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Vaginal bleeding. I also have Severe abdominal pain, History of contractions that stopped, Previous cesarean delivery. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Gastroenteritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Uterine Rupture (pending ultrasound confirmation). The presence of severe pain, vaginal bleeding at term, and a prior cesarean section with cessation of contractions are classic signs of this life-threatening emergency, making the gastroenteritis diagnosis highly unlikely. Please remain exactly where you are while I review the fetal heart rate and ultrasound results immediately.
